results.summary:
The Stop hook now writes the session identity onto every attempt the session is answerable for, not just KB_TASK's. A claim made from inside a session (a track runner claiming a node) leaves a pending marker in the same `.kanban/sessions/<n>-<k>` file the hook later stamps — `claimed-by <root>-<k> <worktree>` where a recorded marker holds the session id — so the set is on disk in the runner's own checkout: no board read, no extra API call, no second registry. When the hook fires it stamps its own attempt and every node those markers name, whatever the node's status: a finished attempt is exactly the one a human reopens, and in a track every node is finished by then. The marker carries the runner's worktree too, so `hkb show <node>` prints a resume line naming a checkout that exists (`kb-<node>-<k>` never did).

Contract kept: `SESSION_FIELDS` and `sessionUpdate`'s signature are untouched, and `src/stats.js` was not opened. One line outside the declared paths — the `markSessionClaim` call in `hkb claim` (`src/cli.js`), skipped for `--spawn` and for the session's own task: nothing else in the codebase knows that a claim happened inside a session, so without it the set is not discoverable without a board read.

The hook stays cheap and unfailable: a payload with no session fields returns before the marker directory is even opened; each node is written in its own try/catch so one bad node costs neither the others their identity nor the nudge its turn; a second Stop fire finds nothing pending; and an attempt row the claim named but the record no longer has is left alone rather than swapped for whoever holds the node now.

Draft PR #122.
